criteria.name: refine_spec_cli_flag
criteria.description: A --refine-spec boolean CLI flag is added to parseCli() and resolveConfig(). When not passed, it defaults to false. The flag is stored as refineSpec on HarnessConfig. Running `bun run cli --help` (or equivalent) lists the flag. Passing --refine-spec sets config.refineSpec to true; omitting it leaves it false.

criteria.name: planner_reinvocation_after_passing_sprint
criteria.description: When --refine-spec is set and a sprint passes (but is not the last sprint), the Planner agent is re-invoked with the current spec content and a prompt instructing it to propose adjustments for remaining (not-yet-started) sprints based on what was actually built. The Planner writes the revised spec to .adhd/spec.md. No re-invocation occurs after the final sprint passes or after a sprint that fails.

criteria.name: completed_sprint_freezing
criteria.description: The refinement logic ensures completed sprints cannot be modified. The spec content for completed sprints (all ## Sprint N sections where N <= current completed sprint number) remains byte-identical before and after refinement. This is enforced by either (a) post-processing the Planner output to restore original completed-sprint sections, or (b) the Planner prompt explicitly instructing preservation — but regardless of approach, a programmatic check compares completed sprint sections before and after and rejects/repairs if they differ.

criteria.name: spec_diff_computation_and_logging
criteria.description: After the Planner proposes spec changes, a line-level diff between the old spec and the proposed spec is computed and logged to the terminal. Added lines are prefixed with '+', removed lines with '-'. If the old and proposed specs are identical, a message indicating no changes is logged instead of an empty diff.

criteria.name: user_gate_for_refinement_approval
criteria.description: In interactive mode, after the spec diff is displayed, a gate is shown to the user with options to Accept or Reject the revised spec. If rejected, the original spec is preserved unchanged. If accepted, the revised spec replaces the current one on disk. The gate uses the existing promptGate/promptGateWithText infrastructure. The gate prompt clearly labels which option preserves the original.

criteria.name: auto_accept_non_interactive
criteria.description: When both --refine-spec and --no-interactive are set, the refinement gate is skipped (auto-accepted) and the revised spec is written to disk, but the spec diff is still logged to the terminal for auditability. A log line explicitly states the refinement was auto-accepted.

criteria.name: no_refinement_without_flag
criteria.description: When --refine-spec is NOT passed, no Planner re-invocation occurs after any sprint passes. The existing sprint transition behavior is completely preserved — no new log lines, no new agent calls, no spec reads/writes beyond what already exists. Verified by: running a multi-sprint loop without --refine-spec and confirming no refinement-related log output appears.

criteria.name: regression_criteria_preserved_after_refinement
criteria.description: After spec refinement occurs (whether accepted or rejected), the accumulated BDD regression criteria in .adhd/regression.json remain byte-identical to their pre-refinement state. Refinement does not clear, modify, or re-derive regression criteria from completed sprints.

criteria.name: sprint_count_recalculation
criteria.description: After spec refinement is accepted, the total sprint count is recalculated from the revised spec (by counting ## Sprint N headings). If refinement adds or removes sprints, the loop's totalSprints variable is updated accordingly, capped by config.maxSprints. A log line reports the new sprint count (e.g., 'Sprint count updated: 5 → 6').

criteria.name: reject_preserves_original_spec
criteria.description: When the user rejects the proposed refinement at the gate, the original spec is fully preserved on disk (.adhd/spec.md is byte-identical to its pre-refinement state), the sprint loop continues with the original spec and original sprint count, and a log line confirms the rejection.

criteria.name: refinement_prompt_includes_codebase_context
criteria.description: The Planner re-invocation prompt includes: (1) the full current spec content, (2) an explicit list of which sprint numbers are completed vs remaining, (3) instruction to read the actual codebase to understand what was built, and (4) explicit instruction to only modify not-yet-started sprint sections and preserve all completed sprint sections verbatim.

criteria.name: refinement_error_handling
criteria.description: If the Planner re-invocation fails (agent error, timeout, or returns empty/unparseable output), the original spec is preserved unchanged on disk, a warning is logged to the terminal describing the failure, and the sprint loop continues normally with the original spec. The harness does not crash or exit due to a refinement failure.

criteria.name: tests_for_refinement_logic
criteria.description: Unit tests exist covering at minimum: (a) completed sprint section extraction and freezing logic, (b) sprint count recalculation from spec content including edge cases of added/removed sprints, (c) --refine-spec flag parsing (present and absent), (d) no-op behavior when the flag is absent, (e) diff computation produces correct +/- output. All tests use Bun's test runner and pass with `bun test`.

criteria.name: type_safety_and_code_quality
criteria.description: All new code compiles without TypeScript errors (`bunx tsc --noEmit` passes). New types/interfaces are added to shared/types.ts where appropriate. No `any` types are used in new code. Functions have explicit parameter and return types. Naming conventions are consistent with the existing codebase (camelCase functions, PascalCase types).

criteria.name: integration_with_sprint_loop
criteria.description: The refinement logic is integrated into the runSprintLoop function in harness.ts, executing after a sprint passes and before the next sprint's contract negotiation begins. It coexists cleanly with existing mid-run steering (C4), regression accumulation (1.1), and checkpoint saving without disrupting their behavior. The refinement step is skipped entirely (not called then short-circuited) when refineSpec is false.
